hints.text: Compute the initial total absolute difference sum and evaluate how much each single element replacement can reduce it.

hints.title: Maximizing Diff Reduction
hints.text: For each index i, binary search the sorted array for values nearest to nums2[i] and track the maximum reduction.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def minAbsoluteSumDiff(self, nums1: list[int], nums2: list[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums1)
        sorted_nums1 = sorted(nums1)

        total = sum(abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(nums1, nums2))
        max_gain = 0

        for a, b in zip(nums1, nums2):
            orig_diff = abs(a - b)
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_nums1, b)
            if idx < n:
                max_gain = max(max_gain, orig_diff - abs(sorted_nums1[idx] - b))
            if idx > 0:
                max_gain = max(max_gain, orig_diff - abs(sorted_nums1[idx - 1] - b))

        return (total - max_gain) % MOD
```

variables: n is length of nums1 and nums2
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every possible element replacement at every index takes O(n^2) time, which exceeds limits for n = 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting nums1 in O(n log n) enables O(log n) closest-element queries using binary search.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate checks both floor and ceiling neighbors in the sorted array when querying nearest element.
